user.title: MMWave Fusion
user.description: Sets up the multi-radar fusion backend. Radars, zones and cameras are configured from the MMWave card itself, so there is nothing to fill in here.

abort.already_configured: MMWave Fusion is already set up.

radar_unavailable.title: Radar {radar_id} is not reporting
radar_unavailable.description:
The entity fusion system `{fusion_id}` reads radar `{radar_id}` from is unavailable, so that radar is contributing nothing. Its targets are missing from the fused view and any zone it covers alone reads empty.

Usual causes: the device is off the network, powered down, or its ESPHome API is unreachable. Check the device's own page in Home Assistant, then its power and wiring.

This clears itself once the radar reports again.

radar_stale.title: Radar {radar_id} has stopped sending frames
radar_stale.description:
Radar `{radar_id}` in fusion system `{fusion_id}` is still online, but its target frames have not updated within the configured staleness window. The device is reachable and the radar module behind it is not talking.

That usually means the radar's serial link rather than the network: a loose connector, a cold solder joint on the UART pins, or a radar module that has crashed. Restarting the ESP does not power-cycle the radar module, so a full power cycle is the usual fix.

This clears itself once frames resume.

radar_calibration.title: Radar {radar_id} may be miscalibrated
radar_calibration.description:
Fewer than one in five targets radar `{radar_id}` reports land inside the room configured for fusion system `{fusion_id}`, measured over at least 100 observations.

That pattern means the radar sees people but the transform puts them somewhere the room is not — usually a wrong position offset, or a yaw that is off by 90 or 180 degrees. Recalibrate it from the mmWave card's calibration tabs.

This clears itself once its targets start landing in the room.
